mainTopic: A כהן who cannot fully serve hands off his קרבן; paying back what was stolen from a גר to the כהנים
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a כהן with his own קרבן. If he is old or sick, he picks any כהן to offer it, but the עבודה and the hide go to the אנשי משמר. רב פפא explains that he can serve only with great effort. That still counts as עבודה, but eating that way is אכילה גסה, which counts for nothing. רב ששת and רב אשי give similar rules, one for a טמא כהן with a קרבן ציבור and one for a כהן גדול who is an אונן. The גמרא questions each rule and answers. Then a new משנה teaches about robbing a גר who dies with no heirs: the קרן and חומש go to the כהנים, and the קרן must be paid before the אשם is brought. The גמרא brings ברייתות proving that the word 'אשם' in the פסוק means the stolen קרן. It is not the ram, not the חומש, and not כפל. Finally רבא gives rules for paying גזל הגר: not at night, not in halves, and at least a פרוטה for every כהן. He then begins a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An old or sick כהן gives his offering to another כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that an old or sick כהן may pick any כהן to offer his קרבן, but the עבודה and the hide go to the אנשי משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן was old or sick, he gives his offering to any כהן he chooses, and its service and its hide go to the members of the priestly watch.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its discussion of a כהן who owns a קרבן. It gives a new case: a כהן who is old or sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A healthy כהן may bring his own קרבן at any time, and the עבודה and the hide are his. An old or sick כהן still chooses which כהן will offer it. However, he loses the benefits, which go to the משמר on duty that week.

keyTerms.meaning: old or sick
the Temple service, along with the rights and benefits that come with doing it
the hide of the animal, which goes to the כהנים
the כהנים of the weekly shift on duty in the Temple

phrases.english: And if he was old or sick –
phrases.notes: "He" is a כהן who has his own קרבן to bring, which the ברייתא was discussing just before this.

phrases.english: he gives it to any kohen he wishes,
and its service and its hide go to the members of the priestly watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section about a כהן's own קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An old or sick כהן chooses who offers his קרבן, but the עבודה and the hide go to the אנשי משמר.

steps.title: What kind of old or sick כהן is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא with a two-sided question. If he can serve, he should keep everything. If he cannot serve, he cannot appoint a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this old or sick כהן? If he can do the service, then the service and the hide should be his too! And if he cannot do the service, how can he appoint an agent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by showing that both possible ways of reading it seem to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules in the ברייתא. Choosing the כהן suggests he can serve. Losing the benefits suggests he cannot. A person can only appoint a שליח for something he could do himself, so the two rules seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the circumstances?
he is able to do
an agent who acts on someone's behalf
appoints, makes (someone into)

phrases.aramaic: הַאי זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה, הֵיכִי דָמֵי?
phrases.english: This old or sick one, what is the case?
If he is able to do the service –
its service and its hide should also be his!
And if he is not able to do the service –
how can he appoint an agent?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה, הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case described in the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling about the old or sick כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he can serve, he should keep the benefits. If he cannot, he cannot appoint a שליח. Neither reading fits both parts of the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב פפא: he can serve only with great effort
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the כהן can serve only with difficulty. Difficult עבודה still counts, so he may appoint a שליח. Difficult eating is אכילה גסה, which counts for nothing, so the benefits go to the משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is where he can do it only with difficulty. Service done with difficulty is still service, so he can appoint an agent. Eating done with difficulty is overstuffed eating, and overstuffed eating counts for nothing. That is why the service and hide go to the priestly watch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge with a middle case. The כהן can manage, but only with great strain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strained עבודה is still real עבודה, so the כהן counts as able to serve, and appointing a שליח works. Strained eating is אכילה גסה, which does not count as eating the קרבן. Since he cannot properly eat, he does not keep the benefits, and they go to the משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: with difficulty, under strain
overstuffed eating, forcing food down without appetite
it counts for nothing
because of this, therefore

steps.whatToRemember: Service done with difficulty still counts as service. Eating done with difficulty (אכילה גסה) does not count as eating. So the old or sick כהן may appoint a שליח, but he loses the עבודה and the hide.
steps.confusionAlert: The same physical weakness counts differently for serving and for eating. That difference is the whole answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule: אכילה גסה does not fulfill a מצוה of eating, while hard effort in doing an act still counts.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is where he is able to do it with difficulty.

phrases.aramaic: עֲבוֹדָה – דְּכִי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק
phrases.english: Service – since when he does it with difficulty
it is still service, he can appoint an agent;

phrases.aramaic: אֲכִילָה – דְּכִי אָכֵיל עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק
phrases.english: eating – since when he eats with difficulty
it is overstuffed eating,
and overstuffed eating is nothing;

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי עֲבוֹדָתָהּ וְעוֹרָהּ לְאַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר.
phrases.english: because of this, its service and its hide go to the members of the priestly watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שֶׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a middle case between the two sides of the dilemma
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן either can serve and keeps everything, or cannot serve and cannot appoint anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can serve only with difficulty. That counts for עבודה but not for eating, so he may appoint a שליח but loses the benefits.

steps.title: רב ששת: a טמא כהן with a קרבן ציבור
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that a טמא כהן with a קרבן ציבור may give it to whomever he wants, but the עבודה and the hide go to the אנשי משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: If a כהן was impure, then with a communal offering he gives it to whomever he wishes, and its service and its hide go to the members of the priestly watch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a new rule that follows the same pattern as the ברייתא, but about a כהן who is טמא and a קרבן ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the כהן's problem is טומאה instead of old age or sickness. Like the old or sick כהן, he chooses who will offer the קרבן, but the benefits go to the משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: ritually impure
a communal offering brought on behalf of all of כלל ישראל

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן טָמֵא בְּקׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר –
phrases.english: If a kohen was impure, with a communal offering –
he gives it to anyone he wishes,
and its service and its hide go to the members of the priestly watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן טָמֵא בְּקׇרְבַּן צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel rule from רב ששת, modeled on the ברייתא's old or sick כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא כהן with a קרבן ציבור chooses who offers it, but the עבודה and the hide go to the אנשי משמר.

steps.title: What case does רב ששת mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. If there are טהורים, a טמא cannot serve at all. If there are no טהורים, the אנשי משמר are all טמאים and cannot eat, so why would they get the benefits?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there are pure כהנים, can impure ones do the service?! And if there are no pure כהנים, do the service and hide go to the priestly watch?! They are impure and cannot eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's rule with a two-sided question, just like it did with the ברייתא. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If טהורים are present, a טמא כהן has no right to serve, so he cannot appoint a שליח. If no טהורים are present, the קרבן ציבור is brought in טומאה, but the טמא kohanim of the משמר cannot eat it. Then they should not receive the benefits, which go together with the eating.

keyTerms.meaning: ritually pure כהנים
there is / there is not
they eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a קרבן ציבור can never be brought in טומאה. The second half of the question assumes it can be brought when there are no טהורים. The problem is only with eating it.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If there are pure kohanim,
can impure ones do the service?!
And if there are no pure kohanim,
do its service and its hide go to the members of the priestly watch?!

phrases.aramaic: הָא טְמֵאִים נִינְהוּ, וְלָא מָצוּ אָכְלִי!
phrases.english: But they are impure, and cannot eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's rule from step 4, using the same kind of two-sided question as step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling about a טמא כהן with a קרבן ציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טהורים are present, a טמא cannot serve or appoint a שליח. If none are present, the טמא אנשי משמר cannot eat, so they should not get the עבודה and the hide.

steps.title: רבא: The benefits go to blemished, pure kohanim of that watch
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question on רב ששת. In this case the only טהור כהנים are בעלי מומין, so the benefits go to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Say that it means the blemished כהנים who are pure, who belong to that same watch.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 5 by describing a middle case. There are טהור כהנים, but they all have a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed only two options: either there are טהור כהנים, or everyone is טמא. רבא points to a third option. Blemished כהנים cannot do the עבודה, so a טמא כהן may serve, but because they are טהור they may eat, so the meat and hide go to them.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים with a physical blemish who may not do the עבודה
ritually pure, so allowed to eat קדשים
'Say', meaning read the ruling this way

phrases.english: Rava said: Say:
to the blemished, pure kohanim
who are in that same watch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question on רב ששת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a third case the question did not consider
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either a טמא cannot serve at all, or no one in the משמר can eat
steps.terutzMaskana: The טהור כהנים are blemished, so a טמא may serve, and the blemished טהורים eat and take the hide
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's case: the טהור כהנים of the משמר all have a מום. The טמא serves, and the blemished טהורים get the benefits.

steps.title: רב אשי: A mourning כהן גדול may appoint any כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that a כהן גדול who is an אונן may give his קרבן to any כהן he wants, but the עבודה and hide go to the אנשי משמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: If a כהן גדול was an אונן, he gives his offering to any כהן he wants, and its service and hide go to the men of the watch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds another case built on the same pattern as the earlier rulings. This time the כהן is a כהן גדול in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול who is an אונן may still offer, so he may also appoint a שליח. But he may not eat, so the benefits go to the אנשי משמר.

keyTerms.meaning: the High Priest
a mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial
the כהנים of the group serving that week

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
If a Kohen Gadol was an onen,
he gives it to any kohen he wants,
and its service and its hide go to the men of the watch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אִם הָיָה כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל אוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case using the same formula as the ברייתא and רב ששת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול אונן may appoint any כהן, but the עבודה and hide go to the אנשי משמר

steps.title: What does רב אשי add? A ברייתא already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב אשי teaches. A ברייתא already says a כהן גדול אונן offers but does not eat or take a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: A כהן גדול may offer while an אונן, but he does not eat, and he does not take a share to eat at night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי by saying his ruling seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already shows that a כהן גדול אונן can serve, which should allow a שליח. It also shows he cannot eat, which sends the benefits to the משמר. So רב אשי's ruling seems to follow automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What is new here?)
takes a portion

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
A Kohen Gadol may offer while an onen,
but he does not eat,
and he does not take a share to eat at night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's ruling as unnecessary
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already says he may offer but not eat, and both parts of רב אשי's rule follow from that

steps.title: The new point: He may also appoint an agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the Torah let him offer only by himself, not through a שליח. רב אשי teaches that he may appoint one.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: when the תורה had mercy on the כהן גדול, it was only for him to offer himself, but he cannot appoint an agent. So רב אשי teaches us that he can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in רב אשי's ruling. The new point is that he can appoint a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission for a כהן גדול אונן to serve is a special leniency. We might have limited it to his own hands. רב אשי teaches that it counts as full ability to serve, so he can also send a שליח.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say
the Torah had mercy
to appoint an agent

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול אונן's permission to serve also includes appointing a שליח. The meat and hide still go to the משמר.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חָס רַחֲמָנָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל –
phrases.english: when the Merciful One had mercy on the Kohen Gadol,
it is for him to offer,
but to appoint an agent,
he cannot appoint one;
so he teaches us that he can.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'what is new' question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point by rejecting a possible mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leniency lets him offer only by himself, with no שליח

steps.title: משנה: Robbing a convert who then dies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who robbed a גר, swore falsely, and the גר died pays the קרן and חומש to the כהנים and brings an אשם, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who robs a convert, swears falsely to him, and the convert dies, pays the principal and a fifth to the כהנים, and brings a guilt offering to the altar. As it says: 'And if the man has no redeemer to return the guilt to him, the guilt that is returned goes to ה׳, to the כהן, besides the ram of atonement with which he atones for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case: stolen money from a גר who left no heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר with no relatives has no one to receive repayment. The פסוק says that in such a case the payment goes to the כהן. The robber also brings an אשם to finish his כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: a convert, who may have no Jewish heirs
the stolen amount plus an added fifth
guilt offering
a relative who would inherit

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who robs a convert,
and swore to him falsely, and then the convert died,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחוֹמֶשׁ לַכֹּהֲנִים,
phrases.english: pays the principal and a fifth to the kohanim,
and brings a guilt offering to the altar;
as it says:
'And if the man has no redeemer
to whom the guilt can be returned,
the guilt that is returned goes to ה׳, to the kohen,
phrases.notes: Here 'the guilt' means the stolen money being paid back, not the animal.

phrases.english: besides the ram of atonement
with which he will atone for him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַגּוֹזֵל אֶת הַגֵּר, וְנִשְׁבַּע לוֹ, וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Robbing a גר who dies with no heirs: the קרן and חומש go to the כהנים, and the אשם goes to the מזבח
steps.confusionAlert: In this פסוק, 'אשם' first means the stolen money that is paid back. The animal offering is the 'איל הכפורים' mentioned separately.

steps.title: The robber dies on the way to Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: If the robber dies while bringing the money and the אשם, the money goes to his children. The animal grazes until it gets a מום, is sold, and the money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was bringing up the money and the guilt-offering, and he died, the money is given to his children. The guilt-offering grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold, and its money goes to communal gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a new case: the robber was on his way to pay and to bring his אשם, but he died first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the robber died before handing the money to the כהנים, the money never left his ownership, so his children inherit it. The animal was already set aside as an אשם, but an אשם whose owner died cannot be offered. So it grazes until it gets a מום, and the money from selling it goes to נדבה.

keyTerms.meaning: bringing up (to Jerusalem)
it shall graze
until it becomes blemished and cannot be offered
communal gift offerings

phrases.english: If he was bringing up the money
and the guilt-offering, and he died,
the money shall be given to his children,
and the guilt-offering shall graze until it becomes blemished,
and it shall be sold, and its money shall go to gift offerings.
phrases.notes: The animal can't be brought anymore, so its value goes toward offerings brought for the whole community.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה מַעֲלֶה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף וְאֶת הָאָשָׁם, וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's laws of גזל הגר with the case of a robber who dies before paying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money not yet given goes to the robber's heirs. The אשם grazes until it gets a מום, then it is sold for נדבה.

steps.title: The robber dies after paying the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: If he already gave the money to the אנשי משמר and then died, the heirs cannot take it back, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave the money to the members of the priestly watch and then died, the heirs cannot take it back from them, as it says: 'Whatever a man gives to the כהן, it shall be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the previous case: this time the money already reached the כהנים before the robber died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the money is in the hands of the כהנים, it belongs to them. That stays true even though the robber's אשם was never offered. The פסוק 'לו יהיה' teaches that what is given to the כהן stays with the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהנים on duty that week in the בית המקדש
the heirs
to take it out of their hands

phrases.english: If he gave the money to the members of the priestly watch, and died,
the heirs cannot take it out of their hands,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן לַכֹּהֵן – לוֹ יִהְיֶה״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Whatever a man gives to the priest, it shall be his.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 11. Here the money was already handed over before death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money already given to the כהנים stays with them even if the robber dies before his אשם is offered.

steps.title: The money must come before the אשם
steps.stepSummary: Paying the money to one משמר and the אשם to the next is fine. But if the אשם was brought before the money was paid, he has not fulfilled his obligation and needs a new אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave the money to יהויריב and the guilt-offering to ידעיה, he has fulfilled his obligation. If he gave the guilt-offering to יהויריב and the money to ידעיה: if the guilt-offering still exists, the members of ידעיה should offer it. If not, he must bring another guilt-offering. This is because someone who brings his stolen item before his guilt-offering has fulfilled his obligation, but someone who brings his guilt-offering before his stolen item has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that the order matters: the robbed money must be paid before the אשם is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting between two משמרות is not a problem by itself. The only problem is the order. An אשם offered before the money was returned does not count. If the animal is still alive, the משמר that got the money (ידעיה) offers it. If it was already offered too early, he must bring a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: name of one משמר of כהנים
name of the next משמר of כהנים
he has fulfilled his obligation
still exists (not yet offered)
his stolen item (or its value)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is NOT giving to two different משמרות. The problem is ONLY offering the אשם before the money was paid.

phrases.english: If he gave the money to Joiarib,
phrases.notes: יהויריב and ידעיה are the names of two משמרות of כהנים, one after the other.

phrases.english: and the guilt-offering to Jedaiah, he has fulfilled his obligation.
If the guilt-offering went to Joiarib and the money to Jedaiah,

phrases.aramaic: אִם קַיָּים הָאָשָׁם, יַקְרִיבוּהוּ בְּנֵי יְדַעְיָה;
phrases.english: if the guilt-offering still exists, the members of Jedaiah should offer it;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא, יַחֲזִיר וְיָבִיא אָשָׁם אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and if not, he must go back and bring another guilt-offering.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַמֵּבִיא גְּזֵילוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ – יָצָא;
phrases.english: For one who brings his stolen item before he brings his guilt-offering has fulfilled his obligation;

phrases.aramaic: הֵבִיא אֲשָׁמוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֵבִיא גְּזֵילוֹ – לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: if he brought his guilt-offering before he brought his stolen item, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from cases of the robber dying to the required order of payment and offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The robbed money must be returned before the אשם is offered. An אשם offered first does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that returning the money comes first, which the next step limits to the קרן only.

steps.title: The חומש does not hold back the אשם
steps.stepSummary: If he paid the קרן but not yet the חומש, the missing חומש does not stop the אשם from being offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave the principal but did not give the one-fifth, the one-fifth does not hold him back.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the previous rule. Only the קרן has to come before the אשם, not the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'money before אשם' applies to the main stolen amount. The extra fifth is still owed, but owing it does not make the אשם invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: the principal: the stolen amount itself
the extra fifth added as a penalty
holds back, prevents

steps.whatToRemember: Order rule: the קרן must be paid before the אשם. The חומש does not stop the אשם.

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְלֹא נָתַן אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ –
phrases.english: If he gave the principal but did not give the one-fifth,
the one-fifth does not hold it back.
phrases.notes: He means the missing fifth doesn't stop the אשם from being offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְלֹא נָתַן אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 13: the order requirement applies only to the קרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not having paid the חומש does not prevent offering the אשם.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads the פסוק: אשם is the קרן, מושב is the חומש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. In the פסוק, 'אשם' means the קרן and 'המושב' means the חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'אשם' – this is the principal. 'המושב' – this is the one-fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that explains the words of the פסוק about paying a גר who has no relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that in the phrase 'האשם המושב', the word 'אשם' refers to the money that was stolen, and 'המושב' refers to the extra fifth. So the פסוק is talking about both payments going to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'that is returned', a word in the פסוק

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
'Guilt' – this is the principal,
'that is returned' – this is the one-fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by explaining the פסוק the משנה cited in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the פסוק, 'אשם' = the קרן and 'המושב' = the חומש.

steps.title: Maybe אשם means the ram
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own reading: maybe the word 'אשם' in the פסוק means the ram of the אשם, not the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not so, and 'אשם' means the ram?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a challenge to the reading it just gave. This sets up the next move, where it will prove its first reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אשם' usually means the קרבן אשם, an איל. So it would be natural to read the פסוק as saying the ram goes to the כהנים. The ברייתא now has to show why 'אשם' here means the stolen money.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps it is only... (introduces another possible reading)
a ram (the animal of the קרבן אשם)

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only:
'Guilt' – this is the ram?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא: אָשָׁם זֶה אַיִל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading that 'אשם' in the פסוק means the קרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Normally 'אשם' means the קרבן, a ram. So why not read the פסוק that way?

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא to ask what practical difference it makes whether 'אשם' means the money or the ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what practical difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the ברייתא to ask a quick question. Both the money and the ram must be brought anyway, so why does it matter which one the word 'אשם' means? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the ברייתא suggested that 'אשם' might mean the ram instead of the money. Since the thief must give both the money and the ram either way, the גמרא wants to know what actually changes depending on how we read the word.

keyTerms.meaning: And for what (purpose)?
A practical difference that comes out of it

phrases.english: And for what does it make a difference?
phrases.notes: He means: if both the money and the ram are brought anyway, why does it matter which one the word 'אשם' refers to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks into the ברייתא's suggestion in step 16 to ask why the two readings matter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between reading 'אשם' as the money and reading it as the ram.

steps.title: The difference is רבא's rule: no returning at night or in halves
steps.stepSummary: Reading 'אשם' as the money rules out the opposite of רבא's rule. רבא says גזל הגר returned at night or in halves does not count, because the Torah called the money 'אשם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to exclude the view of רבא. רבא said: if someone returned גזל הגר at night, he has not fulfilled his obligation. If he returned it in halves, he has not fulfilled his obligation. What is the reason? The תורה called it 'אשם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. If the money is called 'אשם', it follows the rules of a קרבן: no night and no halves. If 'אשם' meant only the ram, רבא's rule would have no source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא compares returning the money to offering a קרבן. A קרבן is not brought at night and is not brought in pieces. That comparison only works if the פסוק calls the money itself 'אשם'. So the question of what 'אשם' means decides whether רבא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to rule out
Something stolen from a convert who died with no heirs, which is paid to the כהנים
Halves, paid in parts
He has not fulfilled his obligation
The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') called it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the wording of the פסוק has a real halachic result: the money takes on the rules of a קרבן.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of רבא,
phrases.notes: He means: if 'אשם' meant the ram, we would lose רבא's rule. Reading it as the money keeps his rule.

phrases.english: for רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: גֶּזֶל הַגֵּר שֶׁהֶחְזִירוֹ בַּלַּיְלָה – לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: Theft from a convert that he returned at night: he has not fulfilled his obligation.
If he returned it in halves, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
What is the reason?
The Torah called it 'guilt-offering'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If 'אשם' is the money, the money follows קרבן rules (רבא: not at night, not in halves). If it is the ram, that rule has no source.

steps.title: The ram is mentioned separately, so 'אשם' is the money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own challenge. The פסוק later says 'besides the ram of atonement', so the earlier word 'אשם' must mean the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק says 'besides the ram of atonement', you must say that 'אשם' means the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא picks up again and rejects the idea that 'אשם' means the ram. The ram is named separately in the same פסוק, so 'אשם' must mean something else: the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says the 'אשם' is given to the כהן, and then adds 'besides the ram of atonement'. If 'אשם' were the ram, the פסוק would be saying 'besides the ram' about the ram itself. So 'אשם' has to be the stolen money, which is what step 15 said.

keyTerms.meaning: When it (the פסוק) says
The ram of atonement, the actual animal of the קרבן
You must say, it must be

phrases.english: When it says, 'besides the ram of atonement',
phrases.notes: במדבר ה:ח. The ram is listed separately, so it can't be what the earlier word 'אשם' means.

phrases.english: you must say: 'guilt', this is the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא after the interruption of steps 17-18 and answers its challenge from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the wording of the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אשם' might mean the ram of the offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ram is mentioned separately ('מלבד איל הכפורים'), so 'אשם' is the stolen principal.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: 'אשם' is the principal, 'המושב' is the fifth
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא reads the same פסוק: 'אשם' means the קרן, and 'המושב' means the חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: 'אשם' is the principal; 'that which is returned' is the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא on the same פסוק. It starts by stating which word means the principal and which word means the added fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא made sure 'אשם' is not the ram. This ברייתא deals with a different question: inside the money, which word is the principal and which is the חומש? Its opening reading is that 'אשם' is the principal.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא:
'Guilt', this is the principal;
'that which is returned', this is the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא on the same פסוק, now comparing the principal and the fifth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the פסוק, 'אשם' is the קרן and 'המושב' is the חומש.

steps.title: Maybe 'אשם' means the fifth
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא challenges its own reading: perhaps 'אשם' means the חומש rather than the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not so, and 'אשם' means the fifth?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests the opposite reading, that 'אשם' is the added fifth. It will soon reject this, but first the גמרא will ask what difference it makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as step 16. The ברייתא raises a competing reading of the word 'אשם'. This time the other option is the fifth, not the ram.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only…, a formula that raises another possible reading

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only: 'guilt', this is the fifth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading just given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אשם' is the קרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as well refer to the חומש, which is also part of the payment.

steps.title: Again: what difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again interrupts to ask what practical difference it makes whether 'אשם' is the principal or the fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, the גמרא pauses the ברייתא to ask why this question matters. This sets up the answer from the משנה in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the principal and the fifth have to be paid in any case. So the גמרא wants to know what halacha changes depending on which one is called 'אשם'.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make? The same question as step 17, now asked about the second ברייתא.

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks into the second ברייתא, using the same question as step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between reading 'אשם' as the principal and reading it as the fifth.

steps.title: The difference is the משנה: a missing fifth does not hold back the offering
steps.stepSummary: Reading 'אשם' as the principal supports the משנה, which says an unpaid חומש does not hold back the offering. If 'אשם' were the חומש, the opposite would be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is to exclude what our משנה teaches: if he gave him the principal but did not give him the fifth, the fifth does not hold things back. On the contrary, the fifth would hold things back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference is the rule in our משנה (step 14). If 'אשם' meant the fifth, then the fifth would have to be paid before the קרבן can be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever the Torah calls 'אשם' must be paid before the ram is offered (see step 13). If the fifth were the 'אשם', the offering would have to wait until the fifth is paid. That is the opposite of the משנה, which says only the principal holds back the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Holds back, prevents (the קרבן from being brought)
On the contrary

steps.confusionAlert: 'אדרבה, חומש מעכב' is not the halacha. It is the גמרא showing what would follow if 'אשם' meant the fifth. The real halacha follows the משנה: the fifth does not hold things back.

phrases.english: To exclude our משנה, as we learned:
If he gave him the principal
but did not give him the fifth,
the fifth does not hold things back.
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 14: the קרבן can be brought even before the fifth is paid.

phrases.english: On the contrary, the fifth would hold things back.
phrases.notes: He means: if 'אשם' were the fifth, the outcome would be the opposite of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If 'אשם' were the חומש, the חומש would hold back the offering. That would go against the משנה, which says it does not.

steps.title: 'His guilt in its principal, and its fifth' proves 'אשם' is the principal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes from the earlier פסוק, 'He shall return his guilt in its principal and its fifth', that 'אשם' means the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says, 'He shall return his guilt in its principal, and its fifth', you must say that 'אשם' is the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא picks up again and rejects the idea that 'אשם' is the fifth. In the earlier פסוק, 'אשם' is tied to the principal ('בראשו'), and the fifth is listed separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'his אשם' together with 'בראשו', the main amount. Then it adds 'and its fifth' as a separate item. So 'אשם' is the principal, and the משנה's rule (the fifth does not hold things back) stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In its principal, the main amount
And its fifth, the added payment

steps.whatToRemember: In the פסוק of גזל הגר, 'אשם' means the stolen principal. It is not the ram, because the ram is listed separately. It is not the fifth, because the fifth is also listed separately. As a result, the principal follows קרבן rules (רבא) and holds back the offering, but the fifth does not.

phrases.english: When it says:
'And he shall return his guilt in its principal, and its fifth',
you must say: 'guilt', this is the principal.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ, וַחֲמִישִׁתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second ברייתא after the interruption of steps 22-23 and answers its challenge from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the wording of the earlier פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אשם' is joined to 'בראשו' (the principal), and the fifth is listed separately, so 'אשם' is the קרן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'אשם' is the קרן, so the חומש does not hold back the offering, just as the משנה rules.

steps.title: Another teaching: guilt is the principal, restitution is the fifth
steps.stepSummary: A further ברייתא reads 'אשם' as the קרן and 'המושב' as the חומש, and says the פסוק is talking about גזל הגר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'אשם' means the principal, 'המושב' means the added fifth, and the verse is talking about robbing a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא that reads the same words of the פסוק. This one adds that the case is robbing a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא agrees with the earlier one about קרן and חומש. What is new is the doubt it will raise next. It will ask whether 'המושב' could mean כפל, the double payment, instead of the חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא teaches
Robbing a convert (who died with no heirs)
The verse is speaking about

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches:
"Guilt": this is the principal,
"that is returned": this is the fifth;
phrases.notes: Both words come from במדבר 5:8, 'הָאָשָׁם הַמּוּשָׁב'.

phrases.english: and the verse is speaking about robbery of a convert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא reading the same פסוק, which will raise a different doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אשם' is the קרן, 'המושב' is the חומש, and the case is גזל הגר.

steps.title: Maybe 'restitution' means the double payment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'המושב' might mean כפל, with the פסוק talking about stealing from a גר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe 'המושב' means the double payment, and the verse is talking about secretly stealing from a convert?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading. Maybe the extra payment in the פסוק is כפל and not the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גנב, who takes in secret, pays כפל, double the value. A גזלן, who takes openly, pays קרן plus חומש. So the question is which kind of taker the פסוק is about.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only
Double payment owed by a thief
Secret theft (as opposed to open robbery)

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only:
"that is returned": this is the double payment,
and the verse is speaking about theft from a convert?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'המושב' as the חומש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'returned' could fit the כפל of a גנב just as well as the חומש of a גזלן.

steps.title: The verse speaks of money paid by the principal amount
steps.stepSummary: The earlier פסוק says 'בראשו וחמישיתו', so the payment is based on the principal plus a fifth, not on double.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says 'He shall return his guilt in its principal, and its fifth', the verse is about money paid according to the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with the פסוק just before. That פסוק shows the payment is the קרן plus a חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בראשו' means the payment is measured by the original amount, the principal. כפל is double that amount, so it does not fit. The פסוק must be about a גזלן paying קרן and חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: When it says (introducing a proof from a פסוק)
In its principal (its original amount)
Money paid according to the principal amount

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of 'האשם המושב' is about a גזלן paying קרן and חומש, not a גנב paying כפל.

phrases.english: When it says:
"And he shall return his guilt in its principal, and its fifth"
then it is about money paid according to the principal
that the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'המושב' could mean כפל in a case of גניבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בראשו' shows the payment is the principal plus a fifth, so 'המושב' is the חומש.

steps.title: Not at night and not in halves
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that גזל הגר returned at night or in halves does not count. The reason is that the תורה calls it 'אשם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he returned a convert's stolen item at night, or in halves, he has not fulfilled his duty. Why? The תורה called it 'guilt'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to discuss a statement of רבא that it quoted earlier. רבא gives two rules about returning גזל הגר to the כהנים, along with his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls the money 'אשם', the same word as the offering. So it follows the offering's rules. An offering is not brought at night or split into halves, so this payment cannot be either.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself (returning to a quoted statement)
He has not fulfilled his obligation
In halves
The Merciful One (the תורה)

phrases.english: The matter itself: רבא said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quoted this statement of רבא earlier, and now it looks at it properly.

phrases.english: A convert's stolen item that he returned at night
he has not fulfilled his obligation.
If he returned it in halves, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
What is the reason?
The Merciful One called it "guilt".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתות and returns to an earlier statement of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גזל הגר returned at night or in halves does not count, because it is called 'אשם'.

steps.title: A פרוטה for every כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the stolen amount is not worth a פרוטה for each כהן in the משמר, the robber has not fulfilled his duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: if a convert's stolen item is not worth a פרוטה for each and every כהן, he has not fulfilled his duty, because it says 'the guilt that is returned', meaning there must be a return to each and every כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another rule about paying גזל הגר to the כהנים. Each כהן must get at least a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'המושב' means a real 'return' must happen. Something worth less than a פרוטה does not count as money in הלכה. So every כהן must receive at least a פרוטה for a real return to have reached him.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as money
His obligation
Returning, restitution

phrases.english: And רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: גֶּזֶל הַגֵּר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
phrases.english: A convert's stolen item that is not worth a פרוטה
for each and every כהן
phrases.notes: He means each כהן in the משמר that is serving that week.

phrases.english: he has not fulfilled his obligation.
What is the reason? Because it is written:
"the guilt that is returned"

phrases.aramaic: – עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הֲשָׁבָה לְכׇל כֹּהֵן וְכֹהֵן.
phrases.english: meaning: only once there is a return to each and every כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule from רבא about paying גזל הגר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each כהן in the משמר must receive at least a שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: רבא asks about the large watch of יהויריב
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a question: what if the amount is not a פרוטה per כהן for the big משמר of יהויריב, but it is enough for a smaller משמר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if it is not enough for the watch of יהויריב, but it is enough...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up a new question from רבא, built on his פרוטה rule. The question continues past the end of this text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משמר of יהויריב had many כהנים. So one amount might give a פרוטה to every כהן in a smaller משמר but not in this large one. רבא is about to ask what the הלכה is in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (raised a question that needs a ruling)
A watch, a group of כהנים serving in turn
A large משמר of כהנים

phrases.english: רבא asked:
If it does not have enough for the watch of יהויריב
but it does have enough...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's פרוטה-per-כהן rule from step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the פרוטה rule is measured by the משמר of יהויריב or by a smaller משמר (the question is finished later).
